Material comparison limits:

- **Random-write superiority is not established by matching workloads.** E70’s separate changed-content result is `256 / (0.01 + 1.31)` = **193.939394 KiB/s**, with an excluded verification interval and close outside timing. It cannot replace the IDF same-content reference or justify removing the 256 KiB cache.
- E70’s sequential-write **200** and dd-write **196.923077 KiB/s** exclude close; the latter was printed as integer `196`. Compare E75’s complete-command values against committed IDF writes. E75’s 33 command hashes and four complete remount payloads independently pass.
- Different LittleFS versions, libc/random sequences, buffering, timing resolution, fresh versus retained allocation state, and IDF PSRAM-disabled versus openvela coalescing prevent an OS-only speedup claim. IDF dd-equivalent also omits NSH and `/dev/zero` overhead.

**Stop further speed chasing** for sequential/dd writes, bulk reads and small-write latency. Preserve E70’s changed-content random-write performance without further acceleration. E75 already exceeds the simple write references including complete-command overhead; old 500/20/30 targets provide no reason to escalate.

One precision correction matters: TCP TX’s host bitrate is **14.871830 Mbit/s**; **14.876672** comes from treating the rounded CSV `30.0` seconds as exact. UDP RX’s 1,470-byte sender excess matches one FIN datagram, and the host’s Server Report confirms receipt of the receiver’s final statistics.

**The three completed cases are usable as simple same-board references.** Recommend **2.466 / 14.872 / 16.337 Mbit/s** for TCP RX / TCP TX / UDP RX. TCP TX needs a small correction from the rough **14.877** value.

The meaningful accounting qualifications are:

- **TCP time rounding:** host CSV intervals have only 0.1-second precision. Dividing TCP TX bytes by printed `30.0` produces **14.876672**, whereas its native bitrate is **14.871830**. Board sender timing independently gives **14.874032**. For TCP RX, host reports **2.465158**, versus board receiver **2.465723**. These small endpoint/timing differences do not imply lost bytes. Use receiver accounting; do not substitute exactly 30 seconds.
- **TCP periodic totals:** TX host interval rows sum to **55,729,884 B**, leaving **57,636 B** present only in the final aggregate. Preserve that reporting discrepancy; use the final aggregate, corroborated by the board total. All three cases reached STOPPED/CLOSED and successful completion; TCP RX ended by EOF, without reaching its cap.
- **UDP FIN/ACK:** sender bytes are **61,371,030**, exactly **1,470 B** above receiver data—one FIN datagram. Receiver sequence accounting is `first=1`, `highest=41748`, `FIN=41749`, `unique=expected=41748`: **zero observed loss**, zero duplicates/stale packets, **129 out-of-order arrivals**. The host’s received Server Report matches receiver bytes/loss/reordering, proving final-report delivery. Board `ack_received=0` is appropriate for its server role; it sent five reports. The textual **“Sent 41750 datagrams”** must not be used as the payload-loss denominator. [Raw UDP host report](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-idf-reference-baseline/measurement-30s-03/udp-rx/stdout.log)
- UDP’s printed **0.000 ms jitter is unmeasured**, not established zero jitter. `40M` is the requested **41,943,040 bit/s** load; actual sender throughput was approximately **16.336 Mbit/s**. Zero loss applies to that achieved traffic.

UDP TX remains **failed host preparation**, not board performance failure: stderr says `listener bind failed: Permission denied`, despite process exit 0. Root’s confirmed excluded range explains port 59443. Retrying only UDP TX on validated port 5001 is sufficient; these completed cases need no retest for this descriptive use. I’ll verify UDP TX’s raw counters, hashes, FIN/ACK report, and source send accounting, then combine it with the three reviewed references. I’ll keep local send failures separate from receiver-reported loss and use filesystem reads only.

**Use 18.97 Mbit/s as the UDP TX goodput reference, with local send failures reported separately.** Its receipt/raw counters and host stdout/stderr hashes match; firmware and installation readback match run 03.

| Case | Receiver basis | Reference |
|---|---|---:|
| TCP RX | 9,650,176 B / 31.309845 s; endpoint bytes equal | **2.466 Mbit/s** |
| TCP TX | Host native bitrate 14,871,830 bit/s; endpoint bytes equal | **14.872 Mbit/s** |
| UDP RX | 61,369,560 unique B / 30.052065 s; **0/41,748 lost**, final report received | **16.337 Mbit/s** |
| UDP TX | 71,133,300 B / ACK duration **29.995512 s** | **18.972 Mbit/s** |

UDP TX recomputes to **18.971718169 Mbit/s**, matching the host’s **18,971,718 bit/s**. The receipt’s derived **18.968880** uses rounded `30.00 s`; prefer the ACK duration. [Raw host report](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-idf-reference-baseline/measurement-30s-04/udp-tx/stdout.log)

The [bound source](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/diagnostics/idf-baseline/korvo-reference/components/iperf/iperf.c:205) increments sequence **before every `sendto`**, including failed calls. It continues on UDP `ENOMEM`/`ENOBUFS`. Accounting reconciles exactly:

- **107,142 attempts = 48,503 successful send calls + 58,639 local send failures.**
- Host received **48,390 datagrams × 1,470 = 71,133,300 B**.
- Receiver-reported missing sequences: **58,752/107,142 = 54.835639%**, printed **55%**.
- **58,752 = 58,639 local failures + 113 residual datagrams**; the residual byte difference is **166,110 B**.

Thus **54.84% is not RF loss**. The remaining 113 are an endpoint-accounting difference whose location/cause is unproven; successful `sendto` does not establish physical transmission.

FIN/ACK is positive: `fin=1`, `ack_received=1`, `ack_attempts=1`; ACK bytes/loss/counts match the host report, followed by STOPPED/CLOSED and successful completion. `ok=1` establishes completion under this instrumentation, **not absence of send failures**. [Board evidence](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-idf-reference-baseline/measurement-30s-04/board.redacted.log:75)

Use these four observed rates for practical same-S31 comparison. Keep **58,639 local failures** and **58,752 reported missing sequences** beside UDP TX; neither becomes an acceptable target. Requested `40M` remains offered load, and sender-accepted **19.013423 Mbit/s** is not receiver goodput. The reported UDP TX jitter is also unsuitable as a network-quality reference because normal data packets lack advancing sender timestamps.

The earlier three cases remain valid. The prior port-59443 bind failure remains a separate host-preparation failure. No completed-case retest or benchmark expansion is needed for this descriptive reference; no stability floor or 300-second acceptance is established.
